summary: Cattaraugus County tower built in 1924 by the state Conservation Commission on Hartzfelt Hill south of Olean; removed in 1973; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel lookout tower with observer cabin
facts.status_note: Removed in 1973; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the site

staffing.status: lookout work ended after the 1970 season

facts.agency: New York State Conservation Commission, later the Conservation Department

events.note: Conservation Commission station with a 60-foot steel tower and observer cabin, funded by local landowners and towns
State purchased land around the tower to establish a radio repeater station for law enforcement (per Wikipedia)
Lookout operations ended at the end of the 1970 fire season as aerial detection came into use (per Wikipedia)
Tower dismantled and removed in 1973; NYSDEC photo taken that year

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Commission report, the 2024 newsletter, the Starr list and Wikipedia give 60 feet (18 m). Two 1923-24 newspaper items give 70 feet, as a plan and as an arrival report. The story uses 60 feet and reports the newspaper figures.
The Starr list and the Commission report say Hartzfelt Hill; Wikipedia and the 2024 newsletter say Hartzfelt Mountain. The story uses Hartzfelt Hill.

notes_for_editor: Name: Starr and the Commission report say Hartzfelt Hill; Wikipedia and the 2024 newsletter say Hartzfelt Mountain. Height: 60 ft in four sources, 70 ft in 1923-24 newspapers; the newspapers may describe the same station under the name Flatiron Rock, but no source says so. The 1967 land purchase and the end of lookout work after 1970 come only from Wikipedia, whose cited source (the NY FFLA searchable list) was not read. The 1973 removal is supported by the 2024 newsletter. Elevation: 2,410 ft (Starr) vs 2,405 ft (Wikipedia), not used. No source describes the site today and no photo with a direct URL was found. The Forest Lookouts newspaper extracts were read as transcriptions; the originals were not checked. Access is not stated in any source, so no access fact is recorded.
